output.title: VOC Letter to Governor-General Willem Arnold Alting Regarding English Ship
output.abstract: This document is a duplicate letter addressed to Governor-General Willem Arnold Alting of the Dutch East India Company (VOC) in Batavia. It discusses the dispatch of the English ship 'Atlas' and includes a respectful communication. The letter highlights interactions between the VOC and English vessels, reflecting the colonial dynamics and maritime activities in the 18th century.

output.title: VOC Financial Management and Trade in Ceylon, 1785
output.abstract: The VOC's financial administration in Ceylon is meticulously managed with great prudence. The Company faces challenges in negotiating with private individuals due to the restricted nature of the local inhabitants. In the previous year, credit was significantly extended to both the Company and private individuals. The smelting of copper is limited by the Ceylonese inhabitants' supply. Goods have been distributed according to a memorandum from the Ministers of the Caab. The Company has been forced to increase interest rates to 9% and send funds from Amsterdam to Rotterdam. The Company seeks sovereign intervention to address unfavorable conditions affecting trade with private individuals. Resolutions for the year 1785 include the distribution of 13 tons of goods and further financial arrangements with the Ministers of the Caab.

output.title: VOC Request for Financial Relief and Land Distribution
output.abstract: The document discusses the VOC's dire financial situation, necessitating urgent assistance. It highlights the dependency on resolutions from the sovereign and the involvement of Heeren Commissarissen for land distribution in India and Ceylon (Sri Lanka). The text mentions the need to divide remaining Indian and Ceylonese goods among respective chambers and to send funds to these regions at the earliest opportunity. The VOC's urgent plea reflects its financial strain and administrative challenges.

output.title: VOC Communication on Logistical Challenges in 1784
output.abstract: This document is an extract from a missive dated November 18, 1784, from the directors of the VOC in the Netherlands to the Governor-General and Council of the Indies in Batavia. It discusses the logistical challenges faced in transporting correspondence and papers, including the loss of the ship 'De Zwaluw' at Padang due to poor condition. The papers were subsequently sent overland to Amsterdam. Key entities mentioned include the VOC, Batavia, Padang, and the ship 'De Zwaluw'.

output.title: VOC Rice Supply and Shankoos Payment Dispute, Ceylon 1784
output.abstract: In June 1784, the VOC received an offer to supply 800-1000 lasten of Bengal or coastal rice annually in Ceylon without payment in shankoos. The VOC accepted 800 lasten at 4 rijksdaalders per zak of 150 lb. The shankoosduikerij was left unpaid that year. The VOC awaits further orders regarding the payment of shankoos, previously to be covered by Blinne or Ross's estate, as per a 1780 resolution. The VOC notes the inability to use similar funds in current circumstances. Correspondence from September 1784 indicates pending review of shankoos payments upon peace restoration.

output.title: VOC Resolution on Lijwaad Pagt Compensation, 1782
output.abstract: This document discusses a VOC resolution from January 15, 1782, regarding compensation for a lijwaad pagter (cloth contractor) in Colombo, Gale, and Kalpettah. The pagter claimed damages due to unfortunate times, verified by visitors. The VOC decided to compensate the pagter with rd:s 7250.36¾, considering the war's impact starting in June 1781. The text also notes arrears from previous years (1776, 1777, 1778, 1779, 1780) that could have been avoided with better oversight.

output.title: VOC Resolution on Secretaries' Compensation and Accountability
output.abstract: This document discusses a VOC resolution from October 1782 regarding the compensation of secretaries in Pale (possibly Palembang). It highlights the delay in paying the 'twintigste' (twentieth part) of their salaries for the years 1775 and 1776. The VOC orders local officials to ensure the payment and holds them accountable for any further delays. The text also mentions the involvement of widows of former secretaries and the challenges in determining responsibility for the outstanding payments.

output.title: 1782 Report on Fort Trincomalle and Defense Works
output.abstract: The document discusses concerns over the state of Fort Trincomalle in 1782, highlighting issues raised in secret communications from April and June. It notes the incomplete defense works and the fort's vulnerability, leading to its capture by enemies. The text mentions the oversight by Ridder Des Roijs de Maat and the need for proper defense preparations.

output.title: VOC Actions During Anglo-Dutch Conflict at Trincomalee, 1781
output.abstract: The document discusses VOC actions during the Anglo-Dutch conflict in 1781, focusing on the strategic decisions made regarding ships and cargo at Trincomalee. It mentions the burning of ships to prevent capture by the English and references secret orders sent by ministers. Key dates include December 5-24, 1781, and February 12, highlighting the urgency and secrecy of the operations. The text also notes the absence of English frigates and the successful evacuation of VOC ships.

output.title: VOC Shipper Iansen's Alleged Deception in the Paalsche Baai
output.abstract: The document discusses an incident involving VOC shipper Iansen and an English vessel in the Paalsche Baai. Iansen was suspected of deception, using others to divert attention from his own actions. The text highlights the use of subterfuge by individuals to avoid accountability. The VOC decided not to pursue the case further due to the absence of Iansen, but the Pakhuismeester's complaints against him were reinforced.

output.title: VOC Ship Movements and Cargo Details, 17th October - 1st January
output.abstract: This document details the movements and cargo of VOC ships, particularly the 'Spaarenrijk' and 'De Liefde'. The 'Spaarenrijk' departed from Pale on 20 November for Koetsjim to load pepper and rice. Despite delays, it was later reported to have sailed from Porca on 23 December. The 'De Liefde' received weekly updates, and the Governor of the bank at Gale confirmed that the 'Spaarenrijk' had departed for Ceylon on 1 January. The document also mentions a resolution dated 11 October.

output.title: VOC Ship Stavenisse Redirected to Amsterdam
output.abstract: A VOC document dated 24th of the current month discusses the redirection of the ship Stavenisse from Zeeland to Amsterdam. The ship, already loaded, was redirected due to the absence of essential personnel, Peeper and Papeeter, needed to load two return ships. Orders were given to load the Stavenisse with soapstone as ballast.

output.title: VOC Ship Stavenisse: Voyages and Cargo Details, 17th Century
output.abstract: The document details the voyages and cargo of the VOC ship Stavenisse. The ship, originally assigned to the Chamber of Zeeland but later reassigned to Amsterdam, arrived in Batavia on October 10th with its cargo unloaded. It then traveled to Koetsjiem and returned with a cargo of rice, pepper, and other necessities. Part of this cargo was unloaded, and the rest, along with supplies for the squadron, was sent to Gale. The ship Middelwijk, which left Batavia earlier, arrived on October 19th, and part of its cargo was also unloaded and dispatched according to resolutions.

output.title: VOC Horse Trading and Livestock Management in Ceylon and Madura
output.abstract: The document details VOC activities involving horse trading and livestock management. It mentions the sale of 288 horses and foals on the island of Delft, including various types such as Persian stallions and native mares. The text also discusses the costs associated with maintaining these horses, amounting to ƒ817.5.8. Additionally, it references resolutions from March 19 and April 4 regarding the collection of coarse livestock (lijwaaten) in Colombo and the Madurese coast, aiming to enhance sorting and procurement. The price of coarse livestock for usable horses was set on July 9, following a proposal from Tutucorin officials.

output.title: VOC Pearl Diving Operations in Ceylon and Tutucorin, 1850
output.abstract: The document discusses VOC pearl diving operations along the Ceylon coast and in Tutucorin. It mentions agreements with the Count of Bijland and financial transactions involving pearls. The text highlights a general settlement and the valuation of pearls, noting that the pearls' value was significantly below market price. A resolution on September 3 decided to account for the pearl diving in Tutucorin for the current fiscal year to meet obligations. The document also references a contract proposal by the Count of Bijland and the potential payment of 800 lasts of rice.

output.title: VOC Regulations on Diving Contracts and English Interlopers in Ceylon
output.abstract: The document discusses VOC regulations regarding diving contracts for pearls (kalpettij) and payments to divers (sjankos). It mentions a decision from October 22 to allow sjankos to pay the same rates as ordinary divers for quantities exceeding 20,000. Additionally, it addresses English interlopers operating under the name Aripposche along Ceylon's coasts, as noted in resolutions from December 29 and August 26. Key figures include Administrator De Bock and Under-merchant De Lannoij in Jaffnapatinam.

output.title: VOC Pearl Oyster Inspections in Tutukorin and Madura Coast
output.abstract: The document discusses VOC inspections of pearl oyster banks in Tutukorin and the Madura coast. Despite initial expectations, few and incomplete pearl oysters were found. A resolution dated December 29 was recorded, and a report was to be given to the VOC directors. Additionally, on November 22, a decision was made to inspect the pearl banks on the Madura coast at the request of Nabab Machmiet Alichan. The document is addressed to Heer Jager.

output.title: VOC Purchases of Trade Goods and Provisions in 17XX
output.abstract: This document details the Dutch East India Company's (VOC) procurement of trade goods and provisions in the year 17XX. Key purchases include Bengal rice from an English ship, and various naval supplies such as rope, sailcloth, pitch, tar, and hemp. The document lists multiple resolutions and dates for these transactions, highlighting the logistical challenges and necessities faced by the VOC in maintaining their colonial operations.

output.title: VOC Spice Trade and Miscellaneous Goods: Purchase, Sale, and Profit Records
output.abstract: This document from the VOC archives details the purchase and sale prices of various spices and miscellaneous goods, along with the resulting profits. Key commodities include tarrioffel (turmeric), nagulen (nutmeg), foelie (mace), nooten musshaeten (nutmeg nuts), and kanneel (cinnamon). The records also list diverse items like copper, silver, tools, and equipment. The document provides a snapshot of the VOC's trading activities and financial transactions, highlighting the significant profits derived from the spice trade.

output.title: VOC Transport and Trade Goods Inventory, 1749
output.abstract: This document from the VOC archives details a transport and trade goods inventory from 1749. It lists various commodities such as textiles (e.g., Suratse, Saffenasche), spices (e.g., pepper, cinnamon), and other goods (e.g., coffee beans, sugar, rice). The inventory includes quantities and types of goods for different destinations like Kormandel and Surat. Financial transactions, including purchase and sale prices, are also recorded, providing insights into the VOC's commercial activities and the economic value of the goods transported.

output.title: VOC Council Resolutions on Spices, Nails, and Salt Transport, 1784-1786
output.abstract: This document details VOC council resolutions from 1784 to 1786, focusing on the sale of spices, the pricing of nails, and the transport of salt. Key points include the pricing of mustaats (cloves) and foelie (nutmeg) in Indian currency, the resolution on the sale of nails, and the financial reports of the Domainen for the fiscal years 1784/85 and 1785/86. Additionally, it mentions the ban on salt transport to the upper regions and its impact on the collection of payments in Putelang.

output.title: VOC Land Leases and Compensations in Ceylon, 1799
output.abstract: This document details VOC land leases and compensations in Ceylon (Sri Lanka) in 1799. It mentions the public auction of domains in Jaffna and Mannaar on August 26-27, and the lease of lands in Colombo, Galle, and Kalpitiya for 20,000 rixdollars on September 3. The text also discusses preferential treatment for bidders who made offers before the general auction and compensations given to specific lessees, including a saltpan lessee in Levaijse and Jaffna lessees involved in clothing trade and customs duties.

output.title: Pagoda Coin Production and Transport by VOC, 1784
output.abstract: This document details the production and transport of pagoda coins by the Dutch East India Company (VOC) from September 1784 to August 1785. The Pagoodsmunterij in Kolomst produced 101,759 pagodas, each valued at 1413 1/130 marks of fine gold. The coins were shipped from the Cape of Good Hope on the ship 'Zes Zusters' and transported overland to their destination. The document lists specific quantities and values of gold transported, highlighting the logistical efforts of the VOC in managing precious metals.

output.title: VOC Gold Transport Records from Batavia and Zeeland
output.abstract: This document details gold transports handled by the VOC, including 54 baharen (a unit of weight) and fragments of gold brought by the ship 'Triton' from Batavia. It lists various weights and assessments of gold, with specific entries for gold bars numbered from 1 to 43. Additionally, it records 15 baharen of gold in a chest from the ship 'Stavenisse' out of Zeeland, with assessments for gold bars numbered 1 to 30. The document also mentions 13 gold bars from the 'kijk' part of 13 baharen, assessed and transported via 'Stavenisse'.

output.title: VOC Gold and Copper Transactions, 1412-1416
output.abstract: This document details VOC transactions involving gold and copper between 1412 and 1416. Key entries include the delivery of gold bars and refined Japanese copper to the Hoofdadministrateur. The text mentions various weights and values of gold and copper, losses incurred during processing, and payments to silver smiths, writers, and smelters. Significant amounts of gold and copper were assayed and recorded, with detailed accounts of the refining and assaying processes. The document also includes financial calculations and reductions related to the transport and processing of these commodities.

output.title: VOC Minting Operations and Silver Works in Fanui and Government
output.abstract: The document discusses the minting activities of the Fanui Mint, which had been inactive and was moved the previous year. It details the melting and minting of silver, specifying the weights and values of different batches. The text also mentions the disposal of worn-out silver items according to resolutions dated April 4 and November 22. Additionally, it notes the transfer of the mint to Tutukorin and the financial details of the operations, including transport costs and profits.

output.title: Commission for Colombo Fortress Works, 1786
output.abstract: A commission was appointed to assess and improve the fortifications of Colombo, as previously done for Pale. Major Paravicini, heading the commission, delayed the work during his stay in Trincomalee. The ship Stavenisse may delay its departure due to extensive work in Pale Bay, allowing time to send a preliminary report to the Gentlemen Directors and High Nobles.

output.title: VOC Regulations for Overseas Operations and Official Conduct
output.abstract: The document outlines regulations for VOC (Dutch East India Company) operations, emphasizing the need for continuous work and preparedness against potential threats. It specifies that Lieutenant Lawe must annually swear an oath of faithful service regarding his treatment of coolies, artisans, and all matters under his engineering department. Strict penalties are threatened for any breach of duty. The text also mentions strategic planning and the importance of maintaining vigilance against enemies.

output.title: Request for Lieutenant Lowe's Annual Timber Allowance
output.abstract: The document discusses a request to the VOC for an annual timber allowance for Lieutenant Lowe, amounting to 150 roepijen per month. It highlights the financial burdens faced by the VOC due to timber and repair expenses in various locations, including Colombo, Jaffnapatnam, Mannaar, and Gale. The text emphasizes the need to provide a reasonable income for employees to prevent them from resorting to unauthorized means to fulfill their duties and oaths.

output.title: VOC Administrative Reports and Audits in 1784
output.abstract: The document details administrative reports and audits conducted by the Dutch East India Company (VOC) in 1784. Key activities include the reconciliation of accounts for the Caffecase administration, monthly reports from the apothecary on medicinal supplies, and audits of workshops and iron magazines in Colombo. Administrative actions in Jaffnapatnam were approved, and various expenses, including those for iron and unsuitable goods, were settled according to VOC resolutions dated March, April, and June. The document underscores the meticulous financial and operational oversight maintained by the VOC.

output.title: VOC Accounts and Disputes in Tranquebar and Colombo, 1784-1785
output.abstract: The document discusses the accounts and disputes involving VOC agents Geeke and Peeke in Tranquebar and Colombo. Key points include the examination of warehouse inventories in August 1784, the dismissal of agent Peeke in January 1785 for final accounting and resolving differences with Captain Luijtenaat De Bellon, who commanded ships on the Coromandel Coast. The text also mentions resolutions dated February 1 and April 4, 1785, and the involvement of the first visitateur Berghuijs.

output.title: VOC Financial Accounts: General Expenses and Profits, 1784-1785
output.abstract: This document details the general expenses and profits of the Dutch East India Company (VOC) for the fiscal year 1784/1785. It compares the financial figures with previous years, noting significant increases in both expenses and profits. Key locations mentioned include Colombo, Jaffna, Jaffanapatnam, and Palo. The document also references the inspection of payroll books and act books, as well as the confrontation of muster lists of native soldiers. Specific financial figures are provided for various commodities and supplies, highlighting the company's extensive trade and military operations.

output.title: VOC Accounting and Supply Records for Ceylon and Nagapatnam
output.abstract: The document discusses VOC accounting practices, including the provision of accounts for Ceylon and Nagapatnam. It references specific resolutions from May, December, February, and March, detailing the allocation of supplies and payments. The text mentions the 'eijsch' (list or inventory) of necessities and the provisional accounting for bookkeepers and medical examiners. The document also highlights the compliance with VOC resolutions and the submission of an inventory for approval.

output.title: VOC Inventory of Goods and Supplies, 1727-1786
output.abstract: This VOC document lists various commodities and supplies, including sugar, bandij (a type of molasses), foelie (a type of cloth), nuts, nails, Japanese staffkoper (copper), tin, pewter, ceramics, linen, rice, wax candles, arrack (a type of liquor), Persian red earth, gunpowder components, and various iron and copper goods. The document spans from 1727 to 1786 and includes quantities and possibly financial figures related to these items, indicating the logistical and commercial activities of the VOC during this period.

output.title: VOC Inventory of Medicines and Timber for Shipyards and Workshops
output.abstract: This VOC document details supplies for shipyards and workshops, including medicinal items and timber. Key entries include various medicinal herbs and compounds such as radix calumba, radix china, and lignum sassafras, as well as timber specifications for shipbuilding. The document also lists quantities of borax, kiaser legger duijgen, and different types of wooden planks and beams for various workshops. The inventory covers a five-year period from 1758 to 1763, highlighting the logistical and supply management of the VOC.

output.title: VOC Inventory and Financial Records from Colombo, 1782-1785
output.abstract: This document is a VOC inventory and financial record from 1782-1785, detailing various types and quantities of timber and other materials. It includes specific allocations for shipbuilding (scheepstimmerwerff), house carpentry (huistimmerwinkel), and gun carriage making (affuitmakers winkel). The document also lists financial transactions and commodities like rice (rijst) and nelie across several locations, including Colombo, Jaffna, Mannar, Tutucorijn, Trincomalee, Batticaloa, and Kalpettij. The text provides insights into the VOC's logistical and financial operations in Sri Lanka during the 18th century.

output.title: VOC Council of Justice on Orphan Masters' Non-Compliance
output.abstract: This document discusses a complaint from the Council of Justice regarding orphan masters in Batavia who failed to comply with their orders. The Council seeks guidance on using coercive measures against non-compliant orphan masters. The VOC authorities clarify that the orphan chambers must adhere to the Council's decisions and can be proceeded against without exception. The document is dated September 3, 1721.

output.title: VOC Education and Training in the East Indies, 17XX
output.abstract: This document discusses the challenges and resolutions regarding the education and training of indigenous personnel in the Dutch East Indies. It mentions a meeting on April 15 and September 6, highlighting the need for better and more suitable educators than those typically found in the Netherlands. The text notes that many recent graduates have had to return to lower classes in the Netherlands. It suggests that drawing only catechism teachers and local schoolmasters from the Seminary can achieve the desired goals, as proposed by the scholarchs.

output.title: VOC Support for Widows and Orphans in Jaffna, 1784
output.abstract: The VOC records discuss the efforts of the Jaffna guardians to support European widows and orphans. In 1784, the guardians proposed using the interest from certain chambers to provide for these individuals, as the deacons were unable to adequately support them. The VOC approved this proposal on May 7, acknowledging the guardians' efforts. The guardians planned to distribute aid without reducing the capital, aiming to cover losses related to the pupils' funds, caused by no fault or negligence.

output.title: VOC Records: Diaconij and Leprosenhuijs Funds and Repairs
output.abstract: The document details the financial state of the Diaconij and Leprosenhuijs funds in various VOC locations, including Colombo, Jaffna, Mannaar, Galle, and Matara. The Diaconij capital amounted to ƒ126161:14.6¼, with significant portions allocated to Colombo (ƒ36882.1.2) and Jaffna/Mannaar (ƒ58185.19.8). The Leprosenhuijs underwent repairs costing rd=s 1709.14.½, with the funds recorded under the August 16 resolution. The Leprosenhuijs fund stood at ƒ31735.17½ as of late August.

output.title: Correspondence on Pearl Fishery Disputes with the Nabab of Tutucorin
output.abstract: The document discusses correspondence involving the Nabab of Tutucorin regarding the inspection of pearl banks and disputes over pearl fishing. Key figures include the Nabab, Governor, and Doctor Dot, an English physician. The text mentions letters exchanged between these parties, including responses and resolutions dated September 22, November 7, and December 12. It also notes the arrival of Doctor Dot in Tutucorin and his role in negotiations over the pearl fishery conflicts.

output.title: VOC Regulations on Titles of Don and Modliar in Jaffna, 1760
output.abstract: This document outlines VOC regulations concerning the titles of Don and Modliar in Jaffna, effective from 1760. It specifies that holders must renew their certificates every six weeks on a 12 rijksdaalder seal, paying an additional half rijksdaalder for expedited processing. Those without these titles are encouraged to acquire them, also on a 12 rijksdaalder seal, with an extra half rijksdaalder fee to the Commandeur. The total cost should not exceed fifty rijksdaalders. The titles pose no inconvenience to the Company's service and are voluntary.

output.title: VOC Governance and Thomas Nagel's Role in Ceylon
output.abstract: The document discusses the appointment of Thomas Nagel, a sworn land surveyor, to bring the lands of Ceylon under the direct governance of the Dutch East India Company (VOC). Nagel's extensive experience and efforts in maintaining order and suppressing a mutiny are highlighted. His sixteen years of service in Jaffnapatnam have given him deep knowledge of the region, making him well-suited to govern the Wanni lands effectively. The text underscores the strategic importance of Nagel's character and expertise in managing the Ceylonese people.

output.title: Negotiations with Governor Coutencheau in Pondicherry, 17th-18th Century
output.abstract: The document discusses negotiations with Governor Coutencheau in Pondicherry. The VOC requested information on missing goods and prices, to which Coutencheau agreed to supply the necessary items but could not provide prices. He offered to deliver the goods against receipt and have the accounting handled by European governments. The VOC accepted this proposal and received some ammunition goods on receipt from the French Government.

output.title: Dismissal of Artillery Lieutenant Heupner as Armory Overseer
output.abstract: The document discusses the dismissal of Captain Lieutenant Klaas Ditloff Heupner from his role as overseer of the armory due to age and increasing physical ailments. Heupner is to continue serving as a captain in the artillery. The text also mentions the inventory of received ammunition and a request to settle accounts with the Dutch Government. Additionally, it references the private trade and commerce, and transitions to discussing personnel matters.

output.title: Concerns Over Arbitrary Arrests and Political Tensions in VOC
output.abstract: The document discusses the arbitrary arrests and political tensions faced by VOC officials. It warns about the dangers of a capricious and bitter chief who can arrest officials at will, disrupting all rules. The text advises caution and vigilance, noting that opportunities for action are present. It mentions Colonel D' Hugonet and the increasing unrest due to conflicts between the Dutch Republic and the Emperor. The arrested individuals' intent to resist the government is also highlighted, with references to reports sent to the Heren Bewindhebbers of the Zeeland chamber.

output.title: VOC Legal Proceedings and Military Concerns in Ceylon
output.abstract: The document discusses legal proceedings against an individual and their accomplices, with the case to be reviewed by higher authorities. It also details daily difficulties with the Luxembourg regiment, suggesting it is ineffective for the Dutch East India Company. The text warns of the dangers of having a large number of soldiers in Ceylon without proper control. A resolution dated September 13th addresses the command of the regiment and provisions.

output.title: VOC Military Supplies and Recruitment in the 18th Century
output.abstract: This document discusses the provision of military supplies and equipment for the regiment of Luyemburg and other troops under the VOC. It details the allocation of surplus funds, the distribution of linens and uniforms from the Pakhuijsen warehouse, and the arming of recruits. The text also mentions the financial responsibilities of the Prince of Luxembourg for certain expenses, as per the Capitulation agreement. The accounts are to be settled annually and submitted to the Edele Achtbare Heeren Bewindhebberen.

output.title: Dutch East India Company Personnel List from Tinkonomale
output.abstract: This document lists VOC personnel stationed at Tinkonomale, including soldiers, musketeers, drummers, and matrosses from various Dutch cities and regions. Notable names include Jacobus Kroese, Nic=t Smit, and Thomas Soijsa. The list also mentions specific detachments and locations such as the Iaffenasche Detachment and Malakka. The document provides insights into the diverse origins of VOC employees and their assignments in colonial outposts.
